questions.q: Where was Jeremiah when Yahweh gave a message to him?
questions.a: Jeremiah was shut up in the courtyard of the guard in the house of the king of Judah.

questions.q: What was the Babylonian army doing?
questions.a: It was surrounding Jerusalem.

questions.q: Why did Zedekiah imprison Jeremiah?
questions.a: Zedekiah imprisoned him because Jeremiah prophesied that Jerusalem and Zedekiah would be captured by the Babylonians.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah would happen?
questions.a: Yahweh told Jeremiah that his cousin Hanamel, the son of his uncle Shallum, would come to him and ask him to buy his field in Anathoth, because Jeremiah had the first right to buy it.

questions.q: What did Hanamel ask Jeremiah to do?
questions.a: Hanamel asked Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, because Jeremiah had the right to buy it.

questions.q: How much silver did Jeremiah weigh out for the field?
questions.a: He weighed out seventeen shekels of silver.

questions.q: How did Jeremiah go about buying the field?
questions.a: Jeremiah wrote and sealed the document, had witnesses testify, weighed out the silver on the scales, and gave the documents of the purchase to Baruch in the presence of the witnesses.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah tell Baruch to do with the documents of the purchase?
questions.a: Jeremiah told Baruch to take the documents, both the sealed one and the unsealed one, and put them in a clay jar so that they would last a long time.

questions.q: What message of hope did Yahweh want to give through this purchase of land?
questions.a: Yahweh wanted all the people to know that people would again buy houses, fields, and vineyards in the land.

questions.q: How did Yahweh make the heavens and the earth?
questions.a: He made the heavens and the earth by his great power and his outstretched arm.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah say Yahweh does?
questions.a: Jeremiah says Yahweh shows covenant faithfulness to thousands of people, and also punishes children for the sins of their parents.

questions.q: How does Yahweh reward people, according to Jeremiah?
questions.a: He gives to each person according to his ways and the fruit of his deeds.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh perform signs and wonders?
questions.a: He performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, in Israel, and among all mankind.

questions.q: How did Yahweh make his name famous?
questions.a: He brought the people of Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terror.

questions.q: What kind of land did Yahweh give to his people?
questions.a: He gave them a very fertile land, which he had promised to give to their ancestors.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do after Yahweh gave them the land?
questions.a: They did not obey him.

questions.q: What three things caused the disaster in Jerusalem?
questions.a: War, famine, and plague caused the disaster in Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to do when the city of Jerusalem was being given into the hand of the Babylonians?
questions.a: He told him to buy a field.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about himself?
questions.a: Yahweh says that he is the God of all flesh, and that nothing is too difficult for him.

questions.q: Why will Nebuchadnezzar be able to capture the city?
questions.a: Yahweh will give him the city.

questions.q: What will the Chaldeans do to the city?
questions.a: They will set the city on fire and burn it, including the houses where the people burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people of Israel and Judah have done since their youth?
questions.a: He says they have only done evil in his eyes since their youth.

questions.q: How long had Jerusalem been provoking Yahweh’s anger?
questions.a: Jerusalem had been provoking Yahweh’s anger since the day it was built.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do to provoke Yahweh?
questions.a: They turned their backs on Yahweh, placed detestable things in the temple, built shrines for Baal, and sacrificed their children to Molech.

questions.q: What does Yahweh promise to do for the people of Judah even though they have been wicked?
questions.a: He promises to gather them from all the lands where he scattered them, bring them back to this place, and let them live there safely.

questions.q: How will Yahweh provide for the people of Judah?
questions.a: He will give them one heart and one way to honor him, and he will establish an everlasting covenant with them.

questions.q: How will Yahweh feel about doing good to his people?
questions.a: He will rejoice over them and do good to them wholeheartedly.

questions.q: Just as Yahweh brought disaster on his people, what else was he going to do with them in the future?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would bring on them all the good things that he had said he would do for them.

questions.q: What will people do with fields in the land again?
questions.a: People will buy fields in the land again.

questions.q: Where will people buy fields again?
questions.a: People will buy fields in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, the hill country, the foothills, and the Negev.

commentary.text: Jeremiah buys a field. (Jer. 32:1-15) The prophet's prayer. (Jer. 32:16-25) God declares that he will give up his people, but promises to restore them. (Jer. 32:26-44)

Jer. 32:1-15 Jeremiah, being in prison for his prophecy, purchased a piece of ground. This was to signify, that though Jerusalem was besieged, and the whole country likely to be laid waste, yet the time would come, when houses, and fields, and vineyards, should be again possessed. It concerns ministers to make it appear that they believe what they preach to others. And it is good to manage even our worldly affairs in faith; to do common business with reference to the providence and promise of God.

Jer. 32:16-25 Jeremiah adores the Lord and his infinite perfections. When at any time we are perplexed about the methods of Providence, it is good for us to look to first principles. Let us consider that God is the fountain of all being, power, and life; that with him no difficulty is such as cannot be overcome; that he is a God of boundless mercy; that he is a God of strict justice; and that he directs every thing for the best. Jeremiah owns that God was righteous in causing evil to come upon them. Whatever trouble we are in, personal or public, we may comfort ourselves that the Lord sees it, and knows how to remedy it. We must not dispute God's will, but we may seek to know what it means.

Jer. 32:26-44 God's answer discovers the purposes of his wrath against that generation of the Jews, and the purposes of his grace concerning future generations. It is sin, and nothing else, that ruins them. The restoration of Judah and Jerusalem is promised. This people were now at length brought to despair. But God gives hope of mercy which he had in store for them hereafter. Doubtless the promises are sure to all believers. God will own them for his, and he will prove himself theirs. He will give them a heart to fear him. All true Christians shall have a disposition to mutual love. Though they may have different views about lesser things, they shall all be one in the great things of God; in their views of the evil of sin, and the low estate of fallen man, the way of salvation through the Saviour, the nature of true holiness, the vanity of the world, and the importance of eternal things. Whom God loves, he loves to the end. We have no reason to distrust God's faithfulness and constancy, but only our own hearts. He will settle them again in Canaan. These promises shall surely be performed. Jeremiah's purchase was the pledge of many a purchase that should be made after the captivity; and those inheritances are but faint resemblances of the possessions in the heavenly Canaan, which are kept for all who have God's fear in their hearts, and do not depart from him. Let us then bear up under our trials, assured we shall obtain all the good he has promised us.
